title: Labour and land in Ghana, 1874–1939: a shifting ratio and an institutional revolution
locator: Accepted manuscript, pp. 1–8 and 15–21, especially pp. 5–7 and 17–20; references inspected. Complete PDF acquired; relevant sections read.
scope_limit: Historical synthesis with original archival work and inherited analyses. No new audit of the underlying annual reports, Hill interviews, land transactions or Austin book. No worker-cohort transition or road-level labour denominator.
evidence_lineage: Austin draws on his Labour, Land and Capital research, Hill (1963), Heap (1990), Wrangham (2004), Cardinall (1931), colonial administrative reports and archives. Transport entrepreneurship in p. 7 partly inherits Heap/Wrangham and the Ashanti 1927–28 report. GHA-S05 directly cites this article and Hill; these are connected historical accounts, not independent corroboration of every claim.

title: The Development of Motor Transport in the Gold Coast, 1900–39
locator: Journal of Transport History 11(2), pp. 19–37; inspected article text through author-associated Academia HTML, especially pp. 25–35 and the associated notes; direct local HTML fetch returned 403.
scope_limit: OCR/text extraction, not a locally acquired article PDF. Used for named road initiatives and enterprise arrangements; colonial descriptions of enthusiasm, profitability and cheap labour are not taken as universal consent, measured net welfare or audited financial returns.
evidence_lineage: Research article based on colonial annual reports, Legislative Council proceedings, PWD reports, contemporary newspapers and later transport scholarship. Austin cites this article. Several numerical and institutional observations share Cardinall, Kay and colonial administrative sources with Austin, so agreement is not a new independent observation. DOI 10.1177/002252669001100202.

title: Forced Labour, Roads, and Chiefs: The Implementation of the ILO Forced Labour Convention in the Gold Coast
locator: International Review of Social History 63, pp. 449–476; introduction and pp. 460–475 inspected, especially pp. 464–471; complete university-repository PDF acquired.
scope_limit: Focuses on administrative debate and legal arrangements, particularly northern road maintenance after 1930; explicitly limited evidence of local remuneration and individual experience. Does not estimate all workers or every road. Later reanalysis GHA-S04 challenges the breadth and chronology of its interpretation.
evidence_lineage: Original archival scholarship using PRAAD Accra and Tamale correspondence, ordinances, budgets and reports; draws on Wiemers, Akurang-Parry and other historians. GHA-S04 explicitly engages this study and the same colonial administrative system; the degree of exact document overlap has not been fully audited. Original archival items are mediated, not inspected separately here.

title: From Forced to Voluntary Labour in Rural Africa: The Transition to Paid Voluntary Labour on the Roads of the Northern Territories of the Gold Coast
locator: International Review of Social History 68(2), pp. 205–231; published online 29 September 2022. Inspected publisher HTML Introduction and sections on labour tax, PWD roads, indirect rule, and people’s roads, with notes 11–113. Relevant extracted text saved; direct HTML/PDF downloads returned 403.
scope_limit: Conservative partial-text label for web-extracted text. Combines administrative records with unstructured 2014–2016 interviews, many concerning later periods. Selected local episodes do not establish countrywide prevalence or individual consent; original interviews and archives not separately inspected. No inference that legislation or international pressure were irrelevant.
evidence_lineage: Original scholarship using district diaries, reports, budgets and correspondence, plus author fieldwork and over 350 interviews described in note 11. Explicitly reinterprets Kunkel and Wiemers; shares the colonial administrative archive context and earlier scholarship, while adding distinct district sequences and later oral evidence. The 1925/1930 PWD and 1928/1937/1945 feeder-road claims use cited contemporary records, not retrospective interview dates.

title: The Permanent Effects of Transportation Revolutions in Poor Countries: Evidence from Africa
locator: January 2015 forthcoming manuscript; §§2–3 background (printed pp. 5–10), §4.1 sample restriction (printed pp. 11–12), §5.1.3 migration discussion (printed p. 18), references; complete PDF acquired. Used for comparison scope and citation lineage, not an independent rerun of estimates.
scope_limit: Same manuscript used as MOB-S08. The main Ghana analysis restricts to cocoa-suitable southern cells. Historical transport summaries require reconciliation with Austin/Heap before constructing a combined modal series. Data, code and appendix estimates were not reproduced here.
evidence_lineage: Original assembled spatial railway/cocoa/settlement dataset and econometric analysis. Historical interpretation directly cites Austin (2007, 2008) and Hill (1963); Austin itself partly inherits Heap and administrative reports. GHA-S01 therefore is not an independent replication of this paper’s rail estimates. Same work/URL as MOB-S08, preserved as a contribution-local source record.
